params.body:
The screen was paternalistic. It decided what the reader could take in: one measure at a time with the other three behind a click, the garage list cut off at twelve, and under every number a sentence explaining what the number meant. Three lines of text in a card two hundred pixels tall.

## Everything at once

**The four measures are a table**, not a choice. Total, the period before, the change, and the day from which that measure has been kept. Four rows of numbers take less room than the sentence that used to explain why only one was visible.

Clicking a row still steers the grid and the garage table, but nothing disappears when you do. That is the difference between navigation and a menu that hides things.

**Every garage, with every measure beside it.** No top twelve. A garage that leads on handlings and is absent on sign-ins is a fact that is only visible when both sit on the same row, and a list that stops at twelve hides exactly the tail that says whether the platform rests on eight garages or on eighty.

**The rhythm is a grid**: weekday by hour, seven rows of twenty-four cells in five shades, with the row total beside it. It replaces a list per weekday *plus* a separate strip per hour, which the reader had to hold side by side in his head to see that Thursday afternoon is the busy moment. The grid says it in one look and takes less room than either of the two it replaces.

A measure without an hour — the daily page counter — gets no grid rather than a row of zeroes that would read as "nobody works at night". It falls back to the weekday bars.

## What went out

`Measures::hours()` and `Measures::dealers()` are gone rather than left lying around: `matrix()` and `dealerTable()` replace them, and the two tests that pinned them now pin the replacements. A tested method nobody calls is still dead code.

## Not taken from the inspiration

The reference screens use spaced capitals for their labels (`SRC DHF DUPLEX INPUT`). The house guide forbids that as a default label, and that rule is there because it cost four redesign rounds on the ProveML sources page. Mono stays quiet: lower case.

Dark was not taken either. What makes those screens good is the density, not the colour, and paper remains the default ground with night as a declared exception.

## Verified

The existing tests followed the change rather than being deleted: every measure must still answer every cut (now including the grid and the table), a daily total still gets no grid, and the date a measure started being kept is now asserted as the table column it became.

New rule R P3-16.13. `npm run build` green, `phpstan` green, `pint` green on the touched files. Local suite: the same nine failures as on a clean `main` in my environment; CI runs on a fresh database.

## Still missing

Drill-down from a cell or a garage to the rows behind it. The grid makes that itch worse rather than better — a dark Thursday at 16:00 now begs to be opened. It needs its own endpoint and panel and it is a better change once somebody has used this for a week.
params.title: Everything on one screen
